Recent indicators suggest that economic activity expanded at a strong pace in the third quarter, but, consistent with Taylor-rule guidance and the Taylor principle, the FOMC maintained a restrictive 5.25–5.50% policy stance and continued balance-sheet runoff, reflecting well-known policy lags and real-time uncertainty (e.g., Fuhrer, 1996; Orphanides, 2001). The emphasis that tighter financial and credit conditions are likely to weigh on activity and inflation aligns with the credit channel of monetary transmission (Bernanke and Gertler), while the note that the banking system is “sound and resilient” suggests lower risk of crisis amplification. Given inflation’s persistence under sticky-information/price settings (Mankiw and Reis, 2002), the Committee’s “highly attentive to inflation risks” language signals a hawkish bias despite the pause. Overall tone: mildly positive (strong growth, no hike) but tempered by elevated inflation and continued restraint.
